content.intro: You'll learn to talk about things that already happened — what you did, where you went, how it was — using the preterite past tense, including the irregular fui/estuve/hice/tuve and the voseo forms you'll actually hear (¿adónde fuiste?, ¿qué hiciste?). The trap: regular -ar verbs stress the ending in the yo/vos forms differently from the present, so 'pasé' (I spent/passed) is not 'paso' with an accent slapped on — the whole conjugation shifts.

vocab.note: Irregular preterite of ir — shares its form with ser, so 'fui a lo de un amigo' vs 'fui feliz' are told apart by context.

vocab.gloss: I was resting / I spent time resting
vocab.note: estuve = preterite of estar, irregular stem estuv-.
Irregular preterite of hacer, stem hic-.
Irregular preterite of tener, stem tuv-.
Voseo preterite of ir — fuiste, not the tuteo 'fuiste' sounds identical here, but compare '¿qué hiciste?' below where voseo really stands out.

vocab.gloss: What did you do this weekend?
vocab.note: Voseo preterite of hacer — hiciste. 'el finde' is the everyday clipped form of 'el fin de semana'.
Regular -er preterite, nosotros form.

vocab.term: Pasé por lo de un amigo
vocab.gloss: I stopped by a friend's place
vocab.note: Regular -ar preterite, yo form — pasé, stress on the last syllable.
Set phrase — 'pasarla bien/mal' is how you say a time was good or bad, not 'tener un buen tiempo'.
'pasado/a' after a day or week name means 'last', e.g. 'la semana pasada'.

exercises.prompt: A coworker asks what you did yesterday. Say you stopped by a friend's place and rested.
targetHints: pasé por lo de un amigo

exercises.prompt: Someone asks ¿qué hiciste el finde? Tell them you made an asado and had a great time.

exercises.audioText: El sábado fui a lo de mi hermana, comimos un asado enorme y después nos quedamos charlando hasta re tarde. El domingo tuve que trabajar así que no hice mucho más.
exercises.prompt: This person just described their weekend. What did they do on Saturday, and why didn't Sunday involve much?
targetHints: fui a lo de mi hermana

exercises.prompt: Ask a friend directly where they went last Sunday, using vos.

exercises.audioText: Che, ¿y vos qué hiciste el finde? Yo casi no salí, estuve descansando todo el sábado porque el viernes llegué re cansado del laburo.
exercises.prompt: This person is asking you a question and also explaining their own weekend. What are they asking you, and why did they stay in on Saturday?
Tell a friend the full story of your last weekend from Friday night through Sunday — where you went, what you did with people, and how it went overall. Use at least three different past-tense verbs.

content.intro: You'll learn to ask a landlord or agent about an apartment — rooms, utilities, and whether the neighborhood is quiet — and to understand their answers back. The trap: 'expensas' means condo/building fees (maintenance, security, common areas), completely separate from the rent itself — asking '¿cuánto es el alquiler?' does not tell you whether expensas are included.

vocab.note: The monthly amount, distinct from 'expensas'.

vocab.gloss: Does it include the building/maintenance fees?
vocab.note: Expensas cover shared building costs — often billed separately from alquiler.
'split' is the everyday word for a wall-mounted AC unit — assume houses/departamentos may or may not come with one installed.
Also heard as 'cuarto' or 'pieza' informally.
Common even in modest rentals — worth asking about if you want outdoor space.
'tranquilo' covers both 'quiet' and 'safe' — Paraguayans use it as the general reassurance word for a neighborhood.
Can mean either a person who co-signs or the deposit itself — clarify which one is being asked for: '¿garantía de persona o depósito?'

vocab.gloss: How many bedrooms does it have?

exercises.prompt: You're calling about a rental listing. Ask how many bedrooms it has and whether there's a patio.
Ask the landlord whether the monthly price includes the building fees, and whether the bedroom has air conditioning.

exercises.audioText: Mirá, el alquiler son dos millones por mes, pero eso no incluye expensas — las expensas se pagan aparte, unos cien mil más o menos. Tiene dos dormitorios y un patio chiquito atrás.
exercises.prompt: The landlord just gave you pricing details. Are the building fees included in the rent, and roughly how much extra do they cost?
You want to know if the area is safe before committing. Ask directly, and also ask what's required as a guarantor.

exercises.audioText: El barrio es bastante tranquilo, hay una comisión vecinal que se encarga de la seguridad. Eso sí, para el contrato necesitamos una garantía de persona, no depósito.
exercises.prompt: The landlord just answered two of your questions. What did they say about the neighborhood, and what kind of garantía do they require?

You're seriously considering this rental. Have a full conversation with the landlord: ask about bedrooms, whether expensas and AC are included, what the neighborhood is like, and what they need as a guarantor. React to at least one of their answers.

content.intro: You'll learn to order a full lunch at a comedor or restaurante — ask about the menú del día, request modifications, and ask for the bill. The trap: 'guarnición' is the generic word for a side dish and does not itself mean fries or rice — you still have to ask or wait to hear which one comes with your plate.

vocab.note: The standard way to address service staff, not 'camarero'.
Asks specifically about the menú del día (fixed daily lunch), not the full printed menu.
One of the most common comedor lunches — the side varies by day, so ask what it is.
General pattern 'sin + ingredient' works for any modification request.
'traer' is used here for 'to come with' on a dish, not literally 'to bring'.
Say this when ordering one dish for two people or a starter meant for the table.

vocab.gloss: Could you bring me the menu?
vocab.note: Voseo — traés, not tuteo 'traes'.

vocab.gloss: What do you have to drink?

exercises.prompt: You've just sat down at a comedor. Ask the waiter what's on today's menú del día.
You decide on the milanesa. Ask if it comes with mandioca, and ask for it without onion.

exercises.audioText: Hoy tenemos milanesa con guarnición, o si no un pollo al horno con ensalada. La milanesa viene con puré, y de tomar tenemos jugo de naranja, gaseosa o agua.
exercises.prompt: The waiter just listed today's options. What are the two main dishes, and what side comes with the milanesa specifically?
You and a friend want to order an empanada plate to split between you before your main courses. Tell the waiter it's to share.

exercises.audioText: Perdón, se nos terminó el pollo al horno, pero todavía queda milanesa. Ya les traigo el pan mientras deciden, ¿algo para tomar mientras tanto?
exercises.prompt: The waiter just apologized for something. What ran out, and what does he offer to bring you while you decide?
Order a full lunch from scratch: ask what's on the menu, choose a dish with one modification, ask a follow-up question about what it comes with, and finally ask for the bill once you've finished.

title: En la farmacia: síntomas y dosis

content.intro: You'll build on the survival basics from earlier and go further: describing a specific minor illness, understanding dosage instructions, and following what a pharmacist tells you about how and when to take something. The trap: Paraguayan pharmacies routinely sell medication that would be prescription-only elsewhere, and pharmacists give dosage instructions verbally and fast — the listening exercises here are the real skill being tested.

vocab.note: Distinct from 'estoy constipado/a' (a cold) — gripe implies fever and body aches, a cold is milder.
General phrase — specify further with 'para la cabeza', 'para la garganta', etc.

vocab.gloss: How many hours apart do I take it?
vocab.note: The essential dosage-frequency question.
Common instruction — contrast with 'en ayunas' (on an empty stomach).
Used for cough syrup and similar liquid medications — 'jarabe para la tos'.
Voseo — the natural way to open a request at the counter, e.g. '¿tenés algo para la fiebre?'
Standard way dosage is phrased — number of pills + frequency.

vocab.term: Tengo tos y me arde la garganta
vocab.gloss: I have a cough and my throat is burning
vocab.note: 'arder' (to burn/sting) is the natural verb for throat pain, more common than 'doler' here.
Worth asking, since many things sold over the counter elsewhere may or may not need one here.

exercises.prompt: You walk up to the pharmacy counter feeling awful. Say you have the flu and ask if they have something for the fever.
You also have a bad cough and a burning throat. Describe both symptoms and ask if there's a syrup for it.
targetHints: tengo tos y me arde la garganta

exercises.audioText: Tomá dos comprimidos cada ocho horas, siempre después de comer para que no te haga mal al estómago. Si en tres días seguís con fiebre, andá a un médico.
exercises.prompt: The pharmacist just gave you dosage instructions. How often do you take the pills, and what should you do if the fever hasn't gone in three days?
You didn't catch the frequency the pharmacist just gave you. Ask them to repeat how many hours apart you should take it.

exercises.audioText: Este antialérgico es en ayunas, una sola pastilla por la mañana, y ojo que te puede dar sueño, así que mejor no manejes después de tomarlo.
exercises.prompt: The pharmacist just explained how to take an antihistamine. Should you take it before or after eating, and what side effect are they warning you about?

Go through a full pharmacy visit: describe two symptoms you have, ask for something for each, ask whether either needs a prescription, and once you're told the dosage, confirm it back in your own words to make sure you understood.
